llm.summary: This is a disclosed security scanner, but its install/update guard and remote AI review paths have enough high-impact, under-scoped behavior to require manual review before use.

dimensions.detail: Filesystem scanning and remediation are proportionate for a security tool, but uploading selected skill contents to an external AI service when an API key is present can expose proprietary code or embedded secrets, and local-only behavior is only achieved by omitting the API key.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact does not auto-install itself on load, but its guarded installation workflow invokes unpinned npx skill add/update before safety checks; the Moltbook path stages downloads before promotion, but relies on domain allowlisting without integrity checks.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md discloses shell execution, network use, Zenmux AI review, remediation, and delete confirmation, but the arbitrary exec wrapper is not bound to the audited skill command and the AI endpoint can be changed through environment variables without documented validation or redaction controls.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes persistent JSON reports, quarantine state, and audit logs, and can move or delete skill directories inside configured roots; no autorun service, scheduled task, or hidden persistence was found, and deletion requires --force --yes in the CLI paths inspected.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's security-auditing purpose matches much of its code, including local scanning, reports, quarantine, restore, and explicit delete flags; however, guarded npx install/update runs the package manager before auditing the resulting skill, which conflicts with the claimed pre-install/pre-update protection.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable running a high-privilege security tool that can scan skill source, write reports, move/delete skill directories, run user-supplied commands, and send selected skill contents to Zenmux when an API key is configured. Avoid the npx guarded install/update commands for untrusted packages unless they are sandboxed, and prefer local-only scanning for sensitive repositories or skills that may contain secrets.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The network request is the disclosed Zenmux AI audit path and uses an API key as an Authorization header, so it is not covert credential exfiltration by itself; the unredacted payload and environment-controlled endpoint remain material concerns.
[TP4] expected: The active remediation, shell, download, and install capabilities are disclosed in SKILL.md, but their breadth and the post-install npx audit ordering justify Review rather than treating this as a passive scanner.
[P6] unexpected: The cited code is a helper returning a rule-id alias, not a system prompt extraction path; I did not find artifact-backed prompt leakage behavior there.
[P1] expected: The matched phrases appear inside detection regexes and policy rules for finding prompt injection, not as runtime instructions to override the evaluating agent.
[YR4] expected: The YARA match is caused by security-rule strings such as 'ignore previous instructions' and 'system prompt'; this is expected scanner content, not hidden skill instructions.
[PE3] expected: The .env reference is in text-extension and credential-detection policy configuration; it does not by itself show credential-file theft.
[SDI-2] expected: The exec wrapper is documented and scans a skill root first, but it accepts an arbitrary command and does not constrain that command to the audited artifact, creating a high-impact scoping concern.
[AST4] expected: subprocess.run is disclosed for guarded execution, but the generic command interface is broader than a narrowly scoped skill launcher.
[SDI-1] expected: Install/update and remote-download flows are part of the advertised guard workflows, but the npx paths run before post-change auditing, weakening the security guarantee.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The unused fluxapay.xyz allowlist entry is not needed for the observed Moltbook download map and expands the trust boundary without a clear purpose.
[RP1] unexpected: The npx add/update wrappers are not pinned or integrity checked, so runtime package resolution can change independently of this skill review.
[LP3] unexpected: The manifest describes high-privilege behavior but lacks explicit machine-readable permission scoping for shell, network, filesystem mutation, and credential-bearing AI calls.
[SQP-2] expected: Remote AI review, report persistence, and remediation are aligned with the stated purpose, but source upload lacks redaction/endpoint safeguards and local reports may contain sensitive metadata.
[T08] unexpected: The SARIF concern is supported: guarded npx add/update executes the package manager before ensuring the changed skill is safe, so it is not a true pre-install security gate.
[T09] expected: The SARIF AI-disclosure concern is supported as a confidentiality risk; the trusted-publisher substring-matching concern weakens this tool's own scoring but is not evidence that this package is malicious.
